messages.subject: tidyLPA usage (larger sample)
messages.body_plain:
First of all, thank you for creating tidyLPA, its really helpful and fun to be able to run these analyses!

Being a beginner to R env., some results made me question myself whether I am using or misusing the package. I also have one additional question (3).

1) I am using tidyLPA on a large sample, ca. 3500 subjects, and every time I use it on the same data (3 variables in the model) I get all results slightly different (BIC, AIC, entropy, etc.) occasionally with more prominent differences and different solutions suggested as best by compare_solutions.
My estimate command looks like this:
                lpa <- estimate_profiles(db, n_profiles = 1:6, models = c(2,3,6))
However when I ran the same command on a 50% random subsample, the results were the same every time.
​Is this a problem with RAM or processing power possibly?
PS.
I suppose it is based in mclust package, which, I understand, is utilized by tidyLPA, as BIC summaries using mclust directly also differ when used on the whole sample
I have also found this https://github.com/data-edu/tidyLPA/issues/126

2) with a 50% subsample, tidyLPA produces fit estimates for every model except model 6 with 5 and 6 profiles, giving a suggestion: "Examine these analyses carefully: model_6_class_5, model_6_class_6 "
I am not sure what is this suggesting..? Are those models too complex to analyze?
PS
In this case mclust shows BIC summaries for all models with up to 9 profiles - but in mclust the models are defined differently, I am not sure how this compares to tidyLPA

3) Is there a possibility/command to obtain the average latent class probabilities table for all classes (not only prob.min and prob.max)?

the packages are updated (using RStudio)
